findings.reason: the section must name `_plan_review_pending` (recovery.py:490) as the existing sweep coverage reader it supersedes, so the two do not drift as the fingerprint becomes section-keyed, exactly the duplicate-owner failure the item exists to catch.
findings.text: §16 replaces the sweep's whole-plan coverage question (`_plan_review_pending`, which returns whether any stored or delivered review matches the current whole-document fingerprint) with a section-granular predicate, but its text names only the gate's call site in `require_plan_reviewed` and says merely "the sweep reads the same coverage question" without naming `_plan_review_pending` as the reader to rewrite, so an implementer can add the new predicate beside the old one and leave two coverage readers over the same store

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §17 consolidates the thirteen store helpers (`_H2_OPEN_RE`, `_SECTION_OPEN_RE`, `_SECTION_CLOSE_RE`, `_matching_section_close`, `_section_heading`, `_wrapper_section_heading`, `_section_body_end`, `_landed_card_span`, `_is_structural_boundary`, `_attr`, `_class_list`, `_element_id`, `_heading_open_tag_with_id`) behind one public reader `plan_headings` plus one projection (`structured_section_spans`), hiding substantial behaviour behind a smaller interface; §16 and §18 likewise collapse four inline spellings of a rule behind one predicate each.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §16 introduces a new section-granular coverage predicate and names the sweep as a consumer but does not name `recovery._plan_review_pending`, the reader that answers the same coverage question for the sweep today.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1477, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 adds one public definition (`strip_tags`) and retires the public `legacy` flag from `plan_fingerprint`'s signature, §17 adds two (`plan_headings`, the machinery predicate) and moves `landed_section_ids` without changing the count, and §18 adds one (the classification predicate); each section states in its own text why nothing public can be retired and §16 states no refusal family is added, so every section adding surface accounts for it.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the design sections (§16, §17, §18) open by naming the existing machinery they extend (`_StructuredSectionSpanParser` / `structured_section_spans` and `_TAG_RE` in `reckon/_plan_html.py`, `_store.landed_section_ids`, `routing.section_record_id`/`section_id_candidates`, `_schema.plan_executable_remainder`, `_schema.is_section_identity`) and specify grep/AST censuses as the specification rather than a hand list, so the reuse map is present and checkable.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the three small public additions (`strip_tags` in §16, the machinery-element predicate in §17, the classification predicate in §18) each sit over machinery that cannot host the caller directly (a regex cannot be called; a 4×- and 6×-spelled comparison is not an extendable object), and each section states in its own interface-accounting paragraph why it is a cross-boundary exposure rather than a second spelling beside the existing one.
